clue.text: Storekeeper needs to look out for doctor

parts.note: 'Ware!' is an old warning cry meaning beware or look out
a houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who has to keep an eye out for the doctor's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: WARE, as in 'beware', is an old call to look out. A HOUSEMAN is the British name for a junior doctor living in at a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A warehouseman works in a depot looking after stored goods, so he keeps the store.

clue.text: French painter's response, say, to summons from Wooster?

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, sounding like the reply

parts.note: 'What ho!' is the reply to a summons from Bertie Wooster, whose greeting it is

explanation.surface: A question about how an artist answers when P. G. Wodehouse's Bertie Wooster calls him.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster, P. G. Wodehouse's comic toff, greets everyone with 'What ho!'. 'to summons from Wooster' tells us which reply; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Watteau was an eighteenth-century French painter of fêtes galantes.

clue.text: Put forward personal opinion, adding to volume?

definitions.meaning: to speak up and state one's view
to talk louder, turning up the volume

explanation.surface: Asking whether speaking up means adding to the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to speak one's mind and to speak louder.

clue.text: Writer's description of certain annuals

definitions.meaning: Thomas ..., the English novelist and poet
annual plants that can survive frost are called ... annuals

explanation.surface: A novelist's account of some yearly gardening publications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annuals' looks like yearly books but means plants; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy wrote Tess; frost-tolerant yearly plants are labelled hardy annuals.

clue.text: Girl played cricket half-heartedly, without loss of power

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: half-heartedly drops one of the two letters at the heart of the word

parts.note: batted means played as a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A girl took her turn at cricket without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' takes one of the twin T's from the middle of BATTED, leaving BATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabated means with undiminished force, so with no loss of power.

clue.text: European leader born in the French island

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of European
in puts the letter for born inside the French article

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: A European statesman born on a French island.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon, born on Corsica and exiled to Elba, haunts the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was first exiled.

clue.text: Quarrel with boss? One gets shafted

parts.note: a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow
a head is a boss or chief

explanation.surface: An argument with the boss that leaves one cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' is not a row but a crossbow bolt; 'with' is a link. 'shafted' looks like slang for cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrowhead is fixed on the end of an arrow's shaft, so it is given a shaft.

clue.text: Top MP introducing college head to sound US planner

parts.note: a provost heads some colleges

indicators.note: sound tells us to hear the name rather than spell it

parts.note: George Marshall, the US statesman behind the Marshall Plan

explanation.surface: A senior politician brings in a college head to consult an American planner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MP' looks like a Member of Parliament but means military police. 'introducing' and 'to' join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A provost marshal is the officer in charge of military police, so the top military policeman.

clue.text: Like wings to contain extremely stylish masonry

indicators.note: to contain means the wing word holds the other letters

parts.note: alar means relating to or like wings

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of stylish

explanation.surface: Wings built around something very fashionable in stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: S and H, the first and last letters of 'stylish', go after the first A of ALAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is dressed, squared stone used for fine masonry.

clue.text: Persevering type identifying Marx's birthplace

definitions.meaning: someone who keeps having a go is one who tries
Karl Marx was born in the German city of ... in 1818

explanation.surface: Reading the label on a determined person who points out where Marx was born.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who tries hard; the other is the German city where Karl Marx was born.

clue.text: Warning state voiced regarding substance floating in sea

indicators.note: voiced says the words are to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: amber is the warning colour of a traffic light, and Greece is a state, run together as one phrase

explanation.surface: An alert about something drifting out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regarding' is a link. AMBER, the warning traffic light, and GREECE, a state, said together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy secretion of sperm whales, found floating in the ocean and used in perfume.

clue.text: Morality play shows fallen woman — Mary? Wrong name

parts.note: Eve, who fell from grace in Eden

indicators.note: the letters of the name are put wrong, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: A medieval drama features a disgraced woman, wrongly named Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' is a link. 'fallen woman' is a crossword favourite for Eve; 'Wrong' gives RYMA, the shuffled name.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyman is the famous late-medieval English morality play about death and judgement.

clue.text: Turn left, following spouses back to front

indicators.note: following places the letter for left after the other piece
the last letter of the word is taken from the back and put at the front

parts.note: wives are spouses

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn left behind couples going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' carries the last letter to the start, making SWIVE, an old word for having sex, which keeps the surface sly.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to pivot or turn round, so the verb serves for the instruction turn.

clue.text: Disconcerted dun agitatedly biting lip

indicators.note: biting means the anagram holds the other piece in its teeth, around it
agitatedly shakes up the three letters of the word dun

parts.note: lip is cheek or impudence, as is nerve

explanation.surface: A grey-brown horse is upset and chewing its lip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitatedly' gives UND, and 'biting' wraps it round the lip word; dun is a dull grey-brown horse colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnerved means rattled, put off one's stroke, which is to be disconcerted.

clue.text: Mulberries rotten: wanting pound refund

indicators.note: rotten fruit is spoiled, so the letters are spoiled into a new order
wanting means lacking the letter for a pound

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A demand for money back on bad fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting pound' removes L from MULBERRIES; 'rotten' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse is to repay, so it is a verb meaning to refund.

clue.text: One lets other ranks succeed to a smaller extent

indicators.note: succeed means come after, so the ranks follow the other piece

parts.note: less means to a smaller extent
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A statement that enlisted soldiers come into a reduced inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One lets' reads as a person who allows something, but it means one who lets property; 'to' belongs with 'a smaller extent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessor is a landlord, the party who lets out a property under a lease.

clue.text: Thus receives a shock, suffering from lead poisoning

indicators.note: receives means the word for thus takes the others inside

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
a turn is a shock or fright

explanation.surface: Someone thus gets a fright on learning they have lead poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead was the alchemists' metal of Saturn, which is why lead poisoning is called saturnism.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine or saturnic describes lead, the alchemists' metal of Saturn, and its poisoning.

clue.text: Hodge's game attracting endless censure

definitions.note: Hodge's means of or like Hodge, an adjective, as the answer is

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, a game

indicators.note: endless says the word for censure loses its last letter

parts.note: stick is criticism or censure, as in 'give someone stick'

explanation.surface: A countryman's sport draws a lot of criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracting' is a link. Hodge is the traditional name for a typical English farm labourer. 'endless' cuts STICK, British slang for censure, to STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hodge is the stock English farm labourer, so what is Hodge's is rural or countrified.

clue.text: Drive over across area set aside

indicators.note: drive is placed over and across the area letter, so around it

parts.note: to repel is to drive back

explanation.surface: Driving back over a piece of land that has been reserved.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke it, setting it aside.

clue.text: Sergeant-major wearing neckerchief, not a musician

indicators.note: wearing means the neckerchief goes round the officer
not says the following letter is dropped

parts.note: a bandana is a neckerchief

explanation.surface: An NCO in a neckerchief insists he is no musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' leaves BANDAN; 'not a musician' wants to be read together, but the A is the letter dropped and only 'musician' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandsman plays an instrument in a band, so he is a musician.

clue.text: Skinflint mostly lagging behind when climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read from the bottom up
mostly removes the last letter

parts.note: dragging means trailing or lagging behind

explanation.surface: A miser being slow at the rear on an ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DRAGGING to DRAGGIN, and 'when climbing' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is a mean, stingy person, so a skinflint.

clue.text: Mad hope, to live in the moon

indicators.note: mad says the letters of hope are crazily jumbled

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A crazy dream of setting up home on the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' gives PHOE; 'the moon' could also call up Phoebe, a moon of Saturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe is a poetic name for the moon, personified as the Greek goddess Artemis.

clue.text: Jumper found in rubbish by river in thick mist

parts.note: bull is nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: in puts the letter for river inside the word for mist

parts.note: fog is thick mist

explanation.surface: A sweater turns up among junk by a misty riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater, but here it means a leaper. 'found' is a link; 'in' puts R in FOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfrog is a large frog, and frogs move by leaping, so it is a jumper.

clue.text: Land in Tripoli by accident

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: Ending up in Tripoli by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripoli is the capital of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a North African country, so it is a land.

clue.text: Speech defect one's found in old record

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the record

parts.note: LP, long-playing record, is an old record
one's reads as one is; I is one

explanation.surface: A speech flaw discovered on a vintage vinyl disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A lisp mispronounces s sounds, so it is a speech defect.

clue.text: It's played in concert, one being broadcast

parts.note: acting in concert is acting in accord
I is the Roman numeral for one
a programme that is on is being broadcast

explanation.surface: Something performed in a concert hall, with one item going out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An accordion is a squeeze-box, an instrument that musicians play.

clue.text: The governor stole outside to get some tea

indicators.note: outside means the scarf wraps round the governor's letters

parts.note: a boa is a long scarf or stole of feathers or fur
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: The colonial governor slipped out to fetch a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, a scarf. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a black China tea, so it is a kind of tea.

clue.text: Like Harry Potter show mounted in base?

indicators.note: mounted in means set into a base, as a jewel is in its setting

parts.note: a bed is a base, as a seabed or the bed of a machine
a spectacle is a show

explanation.surface: A display set up on a stand asking what the boy wizard looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Potter, J. K. Rowling's boy wizard, is known for his round glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter wears round glasses, so he is spectacled.
